The memo

Verdict is proceed_after_site_check: Leading Pedestrian Interval is proceed_after_site_check and Dedicated Left- and Right-Turn Lanes at Intersections is proceed_after_site_check, each conditional on confirming turning movement and lane room. The corner shows pedestrian and cyclist harm with city evidence for LPI but cost unstated, backplates as best low-cost alternative, under NYC DOT ownership.

Lafayette Street & East Houston Street had 13 injury crashes since 2021-10-31: 3 pedestrians injured, 5 cyclists injured and 1 person killed. [D4]
7% of crashes here had oversized vehicle recorded as a contributing factor, against 1% at the city's priority junctions. [D2]
Leading Pedestrian Interval is expected to avoid about 0.1 crashes a year, worth $27,000 a year with break-even cost $188,000, holding only if the site shows a turning movement. [D7]
Dedicated turn-lane work would avoid about 1.2 crashes a year, worth $427,000 a year, holding only if the site shows a turning movement and room for a turn lane. [D4]
City Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: pedestrian injury crashes changed -17% (95% interval -22% to -11%) at 1,651 sites, and a placebo date shows nothing. [D8]
Backplates with Retroreflective Borders would avoid about 0.4 crashes a year, worth $134,000 a year. [D4]
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $890,000 a year (injury crashes only: deaths are not valued in this figure). [D4]
The NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is responsible for Lafayette Street, East Houston Street. [D5]
Part	Verdict
Leading Pedestrian Interval	proceed only after a site check confirms what the estimate assumes
Dedicated Left- and Right-Turn Lanes at Intersections	proceed only after a site check confirms what the estimate assumes
The case against this verdict (4)

Muse Spark Open argued against the verdict. Code kept an objection only if its fact is in the record.

O1 LPI targets only pedestrian injury crashes (0.6/year) but most harm is broader: 1 fatality and 13 injury crashes including 5 cyclist-injured, which LPI does not address. [D4: crashes.any_killed = 1]
Answer: LPI is expected to avoid about 0.1 crashes a year from its pedestrian target, so broader cyclist and fatal harm remains outside that estimate; verdict stays conditional on site check. [D7]
O2 Pattern shows crashes over-represented for oversized vehicle, not turning conflicts LPI addresses, undermining site-fit for the LPI assumption. [D2: over_represented.0.pattern = factor: oversized vehicle]
Answer: 7% of crashes here had oversized vehicle recorded versus 1% at priority junctions, which does not match a turning-conflict pattern and leaves site fit to be confirmed. [D2]
O3 Cost is not stated, so even the low break-even of $188k for LPI cannot be verified against benefit and turn-lane reconstruction costs are unbounded. [D1: cost_covers = not stated]
Answer: Cost is not stated and the LPI break-even cost is $188,000 with $27,000 harm avoided a year, so cost cannot be verified against benefit. [D7]
O4 Both treatments require site confirmation of turning movement and room for lane; without geometric check, estimates are speculative. [D4: options.4.verify_on_site = a turning movement; room for a turn lane on the approach]
Answer: Both estimates hold only if the site shows a turning movement and, for the turn lane, room for a turn lane on the approach, so a geometric check is required. [D7]

run_2_corner_after_letter_fixes.letter:
To: the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT)
Cc: Council Member, District 2, New York City Council; Manhattan Community Board 2
Subject: Request for safety review at Lafayette Street & East Houston Street

Dear colleagues at NYC DOT,

We are writing to ask for a safety study at Lafayette Street & East Houston Street on the roads you are responsible for.

The official record for the 5 years from 31 October 2021 shows 41 crashes, of which 13 were injury crashes. Three pedestrians and 5 cyclists were injured and 1 person was killed. The yearly cost of the harm is $0.9 million a year in the U.S. DOT's official values for the cost of crashes (2024 dollars). No safety work is recorded in this period. The last recorded nearby project was East Houston Street at Crosby Street in 2015.

We ask you to study and, where suitable, install:
- reflective backplates on the traffic signals, which is expected to prevent about 0.4 injury crashes a year.
- longer yellow signal times, which is expected to prevent about 0.2 injury crashes a year, if a check on site shows the current yellow plus all-red time is below the ITE recommended practice.

In this city, where the city installed a leading pedestrian interval (a walk signal a few seconds before the green) at 1,651 intersections, pedestrian injury crashes fell 17% (95% interval 11% to 22%) compared with intersections that got it later; a stricter check against fake programs is less certain. Please consider this treatment, which must be checked on site for a turning movement.

Thank you for considering these low-cost fixes.

Yours sincerely,
[Your name]
[Your organisation or address]

Sources:
- NYC Open Data, Motor Vehicle Collisions - Crashes (h9gi-nx95)
- NYC DOT Street Improvement Projects (corridors); NYC DOT Street Improvement Projects (intersections); NYC Vision Zero View, Enhanced Crossings (6ax4-q5k4); NYC Vision Zero View, Leading Pedestrian Interval Signals; NYC Vision Zero View, Signal Timing/25 MPH Retiming; NYC Vision Zero View, Speed Humps (jknp-skuy); NYC Vision Zero View, Turn Traffic Calming; NYC Vision Zero priority corridors; NYC Vision Zero priority intersections
- FHWA CMF Clearinghouse, CMF 1410 (reflective backplates on the traffic signals)
- FHWA CMF Clearinghouse, CMF 4219 (longer yellow signal times)
